cf.title: "variable not found in subplan target list", DISTINCT agg over Gather`

input.subject: BUG #19804: "variable not found in subplan target list", DISTINCT agg over Gather`

verdict_reasoning: The bug is real, reproducible on 16 through master, and the patch follows the direction suggested in message #3. Two fixable level 2 points survive, and neither argues against the fix. standards-compat-1 asks which working plans the stricter relation_can_be_sorted_early() check loses, and replication-ondisk-1 asks what the paths.h change means for back branches. Both need a committer who knows the planner to settle scope per branch.

brief.title: Fix sort EC member choice when Gather child computes expressions
brief.problem: A query with a presorted DISTINCT or ORDER BY aggregate fails at plan time with "variable not found in subplan target list" when a Gather sits under the sort. The planner picks EC member b.y as computable because it appears inside the child output b.y * 2, but the child does not output b.y. The report reproduces this on 16 through master, while 14 returns no rows.
brief.proposed_design: prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() gets an explicit list of Vars and quasi-Vars that the input independently supplies, and find_computable_ec_member() stays unchanged. Append and MergeAppend build and attach their children before sort columns are prepared, with column positions taken from the parent targetlist and checked against every child. relation_can_be_sorted_early() considers only Vars and quasi-Vars that are exposed on their own.
user_visible_surface: prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() gets a changed signature for the explicit input list, visible to extensions that call it.
One existing partition_join EXPLAIN output now shows an equivalent EC member as its sort key.
author_claims: The patch fixes the reported query.
All regression tests pass with assertions enabled.
The relation_can_be_sorted_early() change is conservative and may reject some valid early-sort plans.
v2 fixes compiler warnings that CI found in non-assert builds.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane found the cause, a hidden assumption in 9f954177, and suggested having the caller supply the input list. Tender Wang posted a WIP patch and v2, but nobody has reviewed either, and the author asks for feedback on local PHV handling.
unclear: The patch does not say which branches it targets, although the bug exists on 16 through master.
The patch does not say whether the prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() API change is acceptable in back branches.
The author gives no measure of how many early-sort plans the conservative relation_can_be_sorted_early() check now loses.
The author does not explain why the nullingrels superset rule for outer-join inputs is correct.

objections.title: Conservative early-sort check may change plans for working queries
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 16.x has a parallel query whose plan sorts early below a Gather, and the query does not hit the bug. After a minor upgrade, relation_can_be_sorted_early() rejects that sort, so the planner picks a slower plan. The user finds out from latency, with no error and no setting to undo it.
objections.argument: Message #4 says the new fallback 'might reject some otherwise valid early-sort opportunities', and no measure of the lost plans exists. The bug spans 16 through master, so a fix will likely be backpatched, and in a back branch a plan change for queries that are not broken is a compatibility cost. The proposal does not separate the narrow crash fix from the broader tightening, or say which branches each part should go to.
objections.author_must_show: Which queries that plan and run correctly today lose an early sort under the new check, and can that part stay out of the back branches?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 itself says the new fallback may reject valid early-sort plans, and the thread gives no example or count. Message #3 expected a change in this function but did not settle its scope or the target branches.

objections.title: Back-branch ABI effect of the paths.h change is not stated
objections.failure_scenario: The fix goes into a 16.x or 17.x minor release with a changed declaration in paths.h. An extension built against the earlier minor release keeps calling the old signature. It may crash or misplan after the server is updated in place, with no rebuild step to warn the user.
objections.argument: The bug exists on 16 through master (message #1), so the fix needs back-patching, but the patch prose does not name target branches. The patch touches src/include/optimizer/paths.h, and the brief lists a signature change that extensions can see. The commit message keeps find_computable_ec_member() unchanged but does not say which exported declaration changes. A committer would likely ask for a separate back-branch variant that keeps existing signatures, for example a new function beside the old one.
objections.author_must_show: Which exported declarations in paths.h change, and what form of the fix keeps them ABI-compatible on 16 through 19?

critic.reasoning: The patch touches paths.h and names no target branches, so the back-branch question stands. prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() is static in createplan.c, so the concern covers only the paths.h declarations, and a purely added function would cause no ABI break.

refuted.title: Header change in paths.h has no stated plan for back branches
refuted.failure_scenario: The fix is backpatched to 16 through 18 with the changed declarations in paths.h. An extension built against the earlier minor release calls a planner function whose signature changed. It then misbehaves, or fails to load, after a minor update.
refuted.argument: The patch touches src/include/optimizer/paths.h, and the brief lists a changed prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() signature as visible to extensions. The proposal names no target branches and does not say whether the back branches keep the old entry points as wrappers. Postgres usually keeps exported signatures stable in minor releases, so a committer would likely ask for a separate back-branch form of the fix.
refuted.author_must_show: Which exported declarations change, and how will the 16 to 18 versions of the fix keep the existing signatures stable?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same paths.h concern and adds that the commit message does not name the changed declaration.

refuted.title: Signature change to prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() conflicts with a back-patched fix
refuted.failure_scenario: The fix is back-patched to 16 through 19 with the new prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() signature. An extension built against an earlier minor release, such as a custom scan provider that calls this exported function, then calls it with the old arguments after a minor update. It crashes or fails to load, and users find out only after upgrading.
refuted.argument: Message #1 reports the bug on 16, 17, 18, 19rc1 and master, so a fix belongs in the stable branches. The commit message changes the function's arguments, and paths.h is among the touched files. The proposal does not say which branches it targets or how back branches keep the old entry point. A committer would likely ask for a compatibility wrapper on stable branches, or a narrower fix there.
refuted.author_must_show: What will back branches 16 through 19 use, and how do callers of the current prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() signature keep working after a minor update?

critic.reasoning: prepare_sort_from_pathkeys() is a static function in createplan.c, so no extension can call it and its signature can change in a minor release. The remaining paths.h concern is covered by replication-ondisk-1.

refuted.title: Stricter early-sort check may lose plans for unaffected queries
refuted.failure_scenario: After a minor update, a query that computes a sort expression from Vars inside reltarget expressions no longer gets an early sort below a Gather Merge. The plan changes to a slower one on a stable branch. The user sees the regression without any change in query or data.
refuted.argument: Message #4 says the relation_can_be_sorted_early() fallback is now conservative and "might reject some otherwise valid early-sort opportunities". That cost falls on every query that uses this path, while the bug needs a rare mix of Gather, partitioning and TABLESAMPLE. The proposal gives no count or example of the lost plans. A planner behaviour change of unknown size is hard to defend in a minor release.
refuted.author_must_show: Which plans that relation_can_be_sorted_early() accepts today does the new check reject, and are any of them seen in the regression suite or in real workloads?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which makes the same point and also asks to separate the crash fix from the stricter check per branch.

committability.owner_note: Tom Lane diagnosed the cause in message #3 and suggested the caller-supplied input list. No committer has reviewed the WIP patch or v2 yet.
committability.liability: The owner signs for planner behaviour on up to five branches: the new input-list rules in createplan.c, the Append and MergeAppend reordering, and any plan changes in minor releases.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a WIP patch and then v2 to fix CI compiler warnings, and asks for feedback on local PHV handling.

priority.reason: A valid query fails with an internal error on all supported branches from 16 up, though the trigger needs a rare plan shape found by a fuzzer. The patch is about 35 KiB in createplan.c and equivclass.c, and review needs someone who knows EC and setrefs behaviour.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Expand applicability of aggregate's sortop optimization
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner keep the index-based MIN/MAX optimization for aggregates with an ORDER BY clause, such as MIN(x ORDER BY x), when the ordering uses the same column and a sort operator from the same btree opfamily as the aggregate's sortop. Later in the thread, Andrei Lepikhov reworked it into an aggregate support function (prosupport) that removes the aggregate's ORDER BY for min/max.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane reviewed the prosupport version and found no documentation for the new support request. He doubted that sharing a btree opfamily justifies removing the ORDER BY clause, given opposite sort directions and plans without an index. He also found no check that the aggregated and ordering expressions match, and questioned whether MIN(x ORDER BY x) occurs often enough to be worth the planning cycles. The original author then closed the entry because the patch had become a different patch, and suggested a new entry for it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also, I am far from convinced that the code is right: the fact that the aggsortop shares a btree opfamily with orderClause->sortop doesn't seem to be enough to justify removing the aggorder clause.

precedents_retrieved.title: parallel distinct union and aggregate support patch
precedents_retrieved.objectors: David Steele, David Rowley, Daniel Gustafsson
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a Parallel BatchSort node, and later a batch HashAggregate, that hash-partitions tuples into shared batches so each parallel worker sorts or aggregates whole batches for distinct, union and aggregate. A later version replaced this with an unbuffered Parallel Redistribute node that sends tuples to workers through shared memory queues, spilling to a SharedTuplestore.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch needed a rebase for many months and the thread stalled. It got no review for two commitfests, and David Steele and David Rowley said the author had not answered reviewers who suggested an unbuffered Parallel Partition style operator. The author posted a Redistribute version in September 2021, but the visible messages show no review of it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Many months on and this patch still needs a rebase to apply, and the thread has
stalled.  I'm marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Don't shut down Gather[Merge] early under Limit.
Reverted commit(s): Fix buffer usage stats for parallel nodes.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert part of commit 19df1702f5.

Early shutdown was added by that commit so that we could collect
statistics from workers, but unfortunately, it interacted badly with
rescans.  The problem is that we ended up destroying the parallel context
which is required for rescans.  This leads to rescans of a Limit node over
a Gather node to produce unpredictable results as it tries to access
destroyed parallel context.  By reverting the early shutdown code, we
might lose statistics in some cases of Limit over Gather [Merge], but that
will require further study to fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: CRC32C Parallel Computation Optimization on ARM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch speeds up CRC32C on ARM with the 3-way parallel algorithm from an Intel whitepaper, using vmull_p64() carryless multiply to combine three block CRCs, with configure and meson checks for the crypto extension. John Naylor later reworked it to use a lookup table and software carryless multiply, which works on any input up to 8400 bytes and also on x86.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The whitepaper says its method derives from Intel patents, and the patent status of the technique stayed unclear. Bruce Momjian said that contributing code is a copyright matter, unrelated to patents, and that the community may have no way to accept patent usage grants. John Naylor returned the entry because the legal status was still unclear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the legal status is still unclear, I've marked the CF entry
Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PATCH] Equivalence Class Filters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds equivalence filters to equivalence classes, so a btree-operator clause of the form "Expr op Const", such as t1.id <= 10, is also applied to the other members of the class, such as t2.id. The planner collects these clauses while it builds the equivalence classes, then attaches each one to the class that contains its expression.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the matching search would cost planner cycles on every query, often for no gain, and that redundant derived clauses could skew selectivity estimates. Robert Haas showed that pushing the inequality to every relation can make execution slower, for example a retest on the inner side of a parameterized nested loop, and that choosing where to apply it is hard. David Rowley then said the patch was not wanted in its current form and that he would not work on it further.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not necessarily opposed to doing anything in this area, but so far
I've not seen how to do it in a way that is attractive when planner
complexity, performance, and end results are all considered.

precedents_retrieved.title: tablesync early exit
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a tablesync worker call process_syncing_tables() before it enters the apply main loop, so a worker with nothing left to do exits early. The author presented it as a small optimization and as a cleaner split of work between tablesync and apply workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila objected that exiting before the tablesync worker receives any message skips changes up to the LSN where the copy finished. That is safe with the current code but would lose changes for the table in a design where the apply worker applies streamed in-progress transactions, which had already been proposed on -hackers. The saving was only the work to receive messages for one transaction, so the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As per my understanding, this is safe as per the current code but it
can't be guaranteed for future implementations and the amount of extra
work is additional work to receive the messages for one transaction.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow partial union-all and improve parallel subquery costing
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build partial paths for UNION ALL so the branches can run under a parallel plan. It also changes subquery costing to account for parallelism, with a regression test and before/after plans for TPC-DS query 5.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the patch during the commitfests. In March 2021 the patch no longer applied, and the entry was set to Waiting for Author. The author sent no rebased patch, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Since no new patch has been provided, marking this Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid computing ORDER BY junk columns unnecessarily
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a projection at the end of grouping_planner() that removes junk columns added only for ORDER BY or GROUP BY, so expensive sort expressions satisfied by an index are not computed. To mark which junk columns can be removed, it turns the resjunk boolean into an enum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the patch changes only the final top-level targetlist, so lower plan nodes still compute the expensive expression and cost estimates do not reflect the saving. He also thought the resjunk enum change was invasive and suggested waiting for the work on unifying index scans and index-only scans. Richard Guo found Assert failures with postgres_fdw and with FOR UPDATE queries, and CFbot later reported test failures with no new version posted.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My basic complaint is that this is a band-aid that only touches things at a surface level, whereas I think we need a much deeper set of changes in order to have a plausible solution.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use wait_classes.h in pg_prewarm
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes contrib/pg_prewarm/autoprewarm.c to include utils/wait_classes.h directly instead of pgstat.h and utils/wait_event.h. The file only uses PG_WAIT_EXTENSION, which wait_classes.h defines.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reviewer tested the patch, found no problems and set it to Ready for committer. No committer commented before the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID"
Reverted commit(s): Add single-item cache when looking at topmost XID of a subtrans XID
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 06f5295 as per issues with this approach, both in
terms of efficiency impact and stability.  First, contrary to the
single-item cache for transaction IDs in transam.c, the cache may finish
by not be hit for a long time, and without an invalidation mechanism to
clear it, it would cause inconsistent results on wraparound for
example.  Second, the use of SubTransGetTopmostTransaction() for the
caching has a limited impact on performance.  SubTransGetParent() could
have more impact, though the benchmarking of the single-item approach
still needs to be proved, particularly under the conditions where SLRU
lookups are stressed in parallel with overflowed snapshots (aka more
than 64 subxids generated, for example).

After discussion with Andres Freund.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The precedent search returned no row about the same or a similar idea. The thread names commit 9f954177 (messages #2 and #3) as the change that introduced the hidden assumption. That is a source of the bug, not an earlier rejected attempt, and the patch keeps its behaviour on purpose. From the prior-attempts angle, no recorded rejection reason applies.
SQL syntax, GUCs, pg_dump and psql are not affected. The only partition_join EXPLAIN change names an equivalent sort key, which seems acceptable on master.

The fix stays in the planner and adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire-protocol state. Plans are not persisted, so pg_upgrade and standbys are not affected. The only concern from this angle is back-branch ABI.

The fix stays inside the planner and changes how sort columns are chosen. It adds no privilege, role, GUC, catalog object or visible data, and it lets no unprivileged user see or do anything new. The query in the report errors out at plan time, so there is no wrong-result leak either. Leakproofness and RLS quals are not involved in choosing EC members for the sort.
The fix itself is wanted and follows the direction suggested in message #3. The objections cover back-branch cost and side effects, and neither argues against fixing the bug.

This is a fix for a planner internal error on 16 through master. No existing feature or extension covers it. Setting enable_presorted_aggregate = off avoids the error for a user, but it does not fix the planner, so the already-implemented angle has nothing to raise.

This is a bug fix for a plan-time internal error on supported branches 16 through master, which 14 did not have. The bug comes from a fuzzer report with a reproducer, and a committer confirmed the cause in message #3. The demand angle does not apply: the users are anyone whose valid query fails, and a correct-results regression needs no proof of demand.
